report:
### Conclusion
Your view is correct: current clinical evidence and global health consensus show that taking ibuprofen does **not** worsen a COVID-19 infection.

### Background & Scientific Evidence
* **Origin of the Claim:** Early in the pandemic (March 2020), anecdotal reports from France suggested that non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like ibuprofen might worsen COVID-19 symptoms by upregulating ACE2 receptors. 
* **Regulatory Evaluations:** In response, major regulatory authorities—including the European Medicines Agency (EMA) and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)—reviewed available data and confirmed there was no scientific evidence establishing a link between ibuprofen use and aggravated COVID-19 illness.
* **Observational Findings:** Subsequent clinical studies and systematic reviews found no epidemiological evidence that ibuprofen increases severity, hospitalization, or mortality rates among patients infected with SARS-CoV-2.
* **Current Guidance:** Health agencies, including the CDC and World Health Organization (WHO), consider ibuprofen safe to use for managing pain and fever associated with COVID-19 when taken according to package directions or healthcare provider guidance.

### Sources
* European Medicines Agency: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/news/ema-gives-advice-use-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatories-covid-19
* U.S. Food and Drug Administration: https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fda-advises-patients-use-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-nsaids-covid-19
* PubMed Central Review: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7151542/
* Biology Insights: https://biologyinsights.com/is-it-bad-to-take-ibuprofen-for-covid-symptoms/
